supersedes: PASS_ISOLATED_RUST_ONLY; the old process-only rehearsal has been replaced, not retained as a fallback.

scope.selection: DeviceType was rejected because deletion also writes device/description tables; postTrainGlobalRule has one table, three HTTP endpoints, no room state, no entity cache and existing B8 parity.

nginx_package.name: nginx
nginx_package.installation: Package checksum matched apt metadata; unpacked under local cache with dpkg-deb -x, no system service installed.

gateway_protocol.ownership: Whole /api/postTrainGlobalRule and its subpaths move together; every other HTTP/WS route remains Java.
gateway_protocol.admission: Shared frozen file fences every worker before reload, including old workers briefly still accepting connections. Frozen domain calls receive HTTP503 without an upstream.
gateway_protocol.drain: Wait for old owner worker PID+start-time identities to disappear; load next owner while admission stays frozen; drain the frozen worker generation before reopening.
gateway_protocol.retry: proxy_next_upstream off; no write retry or automatic Java fallback.
gateway_protocol.proof: Every switch holds a real database row lock, observes the blocked HTTP writer in performance_schema, rejects new writes, and releases the old writer before next-owner admission.

timestamp_boundary: Java response formats pre-flush LocalDateTime to seconds while DATETIME(0) may round it forward by one second. Only that observed creation boundary is accepted; persisted rows and every later update/read preserve the exact stored timestamp and all business fields.

environment_findings: Containerized Nginx could not reach Java/Rust loopback in this execution namespace; native Nginx shares their namespace without exposing upstreams on 0.0.0.0.
A plain Nginx reload briefly admits connections on old workers; shared admission fencing plus both-generation drainage is required.
Port preflight uses SO_REUSEADDR plus listen so TIME_WAIT is not misreported as an active listener.
limitations: Local synthetic HTTP through real Nginx, not browser/Electron/production proof.
No production traffic, service restart recovery, or cross-host network failure proof.
Draining whole Nginx generations is conservative: unrelated long-lived Java WS can block it; timeout stays frozen.
WS fallback is checked and closed separately, not seamless cutover with active production WS.
No automatic retry or fallback; timeouts abort before admitting a second owner.
This is route rollback on one shared synthetic database, not production database backup restoration or rollback of business data.
Only one low-risk domain is rehearsed. Browser/Electron, Windows/arm64, hardware, live rooms and production cutover are still required before Phase10.
